title: Amazing Grace (arranged for beginners)
subtitle: Hymn tune "New Britain", simple two-hand setting in 3/4
trains: A well-known pentatonic melody with a one-beat pickup, mostly half and dotted-half notes, over a single sustained bass note per bar - gentle two-hand reading at a slow tempo.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: The tune "New Britain" is a pentatonic American folk/shape-note melody of unknown authorship, first published in Columbian Harmony (1829) and paired with John Newton's 1779 text "Amazing Grace" in William Walker's The Southern Harmony (1835) - both public domain. Verified via Wikipedia's "New Britain (tune)" entry and hymnary.org's tune record, which both confirm the pentatonic character (built from the scale degrees 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 only) and the 1829/1835 publication history.
provenance.note: Four 4-bar phrases (16 bars) plus a one-beat pickup, key of G major, quarter=72. The source tune's characteristic long-short (dotted-quarter/eighth) hymn rhythm is smoothed here to plain quarter and half/dotted-half notes so the shortest value and tempo stay inside the Beginner caps; the melodic contour and pentatonic pitch content follow the verified tune closely. The left-hand single bass note per bar (I-IV-V harmonisation) is our own simple setting.
